children.name: tutorial
children.description: guided walkthrough that teaches a user to drive crouter
children.whenToUse: a user is new to crouter and needs to learn to operate it, or an experienced user wants the runtime model behind orchestration and node lifecycles. Distinct from `crtr sys setup`, which installs providers and dependencies but teaches nothing — a user can finish setup and still be unable to open the menu.
children.summary: the crouter tutorial — hands-on lessons an agent teaches, one per invocation
children.model: Two tracks. `basic` makes a user able to drive crouter at all: the terminal and tmux setup every keybinding depends on, the Alt+C menu, resuming, memory, the graph, and the inbox. `advanced` explains the runtime model — orchestration and node lifecycles — and assumes the basics. You are the teacher and each track leaf is a prompt server: it hands you one lesson of instructions and holds no progress state, so `--step` skips freely. Lessons that change the machine tell YOU to make the edit with the user watching a diff; the command itself never writes anything. `scenario` builds disposable canvas state for the two lessons that need something real to point at.

children.name: basic
children.description: teach a first-time user to drive crouter, one lesson per invocation
children.whenToUse: a user is new to crouter and needs to be able to actually operate it — the terminal and tmux setup every keybinding depends on, the Alt+C menu, resuming a conversation, memory, the graph, and the inbox. Run this before any advanced material; it is the track that turns a fresh install into a usable one. Invoke with no arguments to begin at lesson 1; each served lesson names the command for the next. Contents: 1. Terminal Option key. 2. tmux. 3. The Alt+C menu. 4. Resuming a conversation. 5. Memory. 6. The graph. 7. The inbox.
children.summary: the first-run crouter tutorial — serves one lesson per invocation, in order

children.name: advanced
children.description: teach the runtime model — orchestration and node lifecycles
children.whenToUse: a user already drives crouter comfortably and wants to understand what it is doing underneath: when to promote a node to an orchestrator, and why terminal and resident nodes end differently. Run the basic track first; this one assumes the user can already navigate and has done real work. Invoke with no arguments to begin at lesson 1; each served lesson names the command for the next. Contents: 1. Promotion to orchestrator. 2. Terminal and resident nodes.

children.name: scenario
children.description: build and tear down demo canvas state for a lesson
children.whenToUse: a tutorial lesson needs something real on the canvas to point at. The graph and inbox lessons both call for one; other lessons do not need this at all.
children.summary: demo canvas state for tutorial lessons — build one, teach against it, tear it down
children.model: A scenario is disposable demo state built for one lesson and removed after it. Everything created is recorded in a ledger, and teardown removes exactly what that ledger names. Scenario nodes are created without a kickoff, so a row renders in the graph but no turn ever runs and building one costs no tokens. Start, teach, clean — a scenario left standing puts demo rows on the user's real canvas.

children.name: list
children.description: list demo scenarios and which are currently standing
children.whenToUse: choosing a scenario for a lesson, or checking whether a previous run left anything on the canvas that still needs cleaning up.
children.summary: list the tutorial demo scenarios and their current state

output.name: scenarios
output.constraint: Each scenario: id, title, what it teaches, what it builds, and whether it is standing.

output.name: standing
output.constraint: How many scenarios currently have canvas state.

children.name: start
children.description: build one demo scenario on the canvas
children.whenToUse: a tutorial lesson needs real canvas state to point at — idle nodes for the graph lesson, a pending question for the inbox lesson. Always pair it with `scenario clean` once the lesson lands.
children.summary: build one tutorial demo scenario — idle nodes or a pending inbox item, costing no tokens

params.name: scenario
params.constraint: Which scenario to build: idle-nodes | pending-ask. See `crtr dev tutorial scenario list` for what each builds.

output.name: scenario
output.constraint: The scenario that was built.

output.name: nodes
output.constraint: Node ids created, for scenarios that build nodes.

output.name: requests
output.constraint: Human request ids, for scenarios that publish an inbox item.

output.name: clean_with
output.constraint: The exact teardown command for what was just built.

output.name: look_at
output.constraint: Which surface to open to see what was built.

effects: idle-nodes: creates three independent nodes with no kickoff — brokers exist, no turn ever runs.
pending-ask: publishes one durable pending request into the human inbox.
Records what was created in a ledger under the user's crouter directory, so teardown removes exactly this and nothing else.

children.name: clean
children.whenToUse: a tutorial lesson using a scenario is finished. Always run it — a scenario left standing clutters the user's real canvas with demo rows they did not create.
children.summary: remove exactly the canvas state one tutorial scenario created

params.name: scenario
params.constraint: Which scenario to tear down: idle-nodes | pending-ask. Cleaning one that is not standing succeeds and does nothing.

output.name: scenario
output.constraint: The scenario torn down.

output.name: was_standing
output.constraint: False when there was nothing to remove.

output.name: closed_nodes
output.constraint: How many nodes were closed.

output.name: canceled_requests
output.constraint: How many pending inbox requests were withdrawn.

effects: Closes exactly the nodes this scenario recorded; nothing else is touched.
Cancels the scenario's recorded pending human requests.
Clears the scenario from the tutorial scenario ledger.
